what_this_is: Every write site found by `git grep -nE "cache(\.put|\.set|\.write)|CACHE\.put|KV\.put|expires" functions/ serverless/ backend/`, plus the other in-memory Map writes in those trees. A site is either GUARDED (pre-write + post-read value assertion through backend/utils/cacheContract.js) or DISPOSITIONED with a dated reason why it is not a read-through value cache. `__tests__/cacheContract.test.js` fails if a new matched write site appears without one of those two entries.

writeSites.detail: Batch path: the write is preceded by `const guard = cache.set(...)` and a 502 is thrown on failure. Reads go through cache.get's post-read guard.
Single path: same pre-write guard and throw; the mini lookup's post-read guard rejects a hollow entry and re-fetches.
Pre-write guard on the document; cache.get re-validates. A missing file caches `null` as an explicit, validated negative hit.
`null` is a legitimate negative hit; the same assertion accepts it on read and any other falsy value is a miss.
Provider result: pre-write guard refuses an empty generation and logs the named missing fields; cache.get re-validates on read.
Deterministic tier, same guard — a cache write is a cache write regardless of which tier produced the value.

writeSites.reason: Rate-limit counter, not a value cache. The entry IS the count; zero is a valid value. There is no upstream to re-fetch and no served payload derived from it. Applying a weather-point assertion here would reject legitimate counters.
In-memory subscription store (a write-through store, not a cache). Its completeness is validated at the HTTP boundary before this line; a miss means 'nobody subscribed', not 'refetch'.
Durable store's in-memory fallback. Documents are validated by the alert store before insertion; there is no TTL and no read-through re-fetch path.
Request-local deduplication Map inside a single query, discarded when the call returns. Not a cache shared across requests.
Firestore batch write, not an in-memory cache. The ingest pipeline validates rows before the transaction; no read-through path exists.
Prometheus gauge `.set`, not a cache write. Process metrics have no isolate equivalent — see Action 21's metrics disposition and Phase 4.
Headers object mutation while building the canonical policy. Not a cache.
HTTP Message Signature `expires` timestamp. Matched by the grep's `expires` alternative but is a signature validity window, not a cached value.
The signature input string embeds the `expires` value from the line above. Matched by the grep's `expires` alternative; it is part of one HTTP signature header, not a second write site.
Immutable route table built once at module load. No writes after construction.
